text: A business unit by itself is just a name and a ledger assignment. What makes it useful is the business functions assigned to it — the specific jobs it's configured to perform.

A business function is a specific process a business unit can carry out: Payables Invoicing, Billing and Revenue Management, Requisitioning, Project Accounting. One business unit isn't limited to one function.

Oracle Fusion supports a shared service model. One business unit becomes the service provider for a function, and other business units become its clients for that function — like a centralized AP team serving several divisions.

Function assignment isn't just descriptive. It directly affects which setup tasks and reference data options appear for a business unit. No Payables function means no Payables setup options show up at all.
Business functions are the specific jobs a business unit performs, and a unit can be a service provider for some functions while a client for others. Next up, lesson twelve: reference data sets.
